subject: Change request: Add capacity + rate adjustment for Orchid AI
messages:
From: Priya Desai <priya@orchid.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@orchid.ai>, Emily Rogers <emily.rogers@orchid.ai>
Date: Sat, 07 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: add capacity + rate adjustment (Orchid)

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. After an internal usage review, we expect Orchid's production traffic to increase faster than the January forecast. We need to add capacity to our Order Form (ORC-2024-0042) to cover an additional ~200k inference units / month starting July 1.

Commercial ask: can Redwood provide an amended orderform that adds the capacity and applies the volume-discounted unit price from the next tier (we were on Tier 2; asking to price the added capacity at Tier 3 rates). We'd like to avoid a full MSA amendment if possible, but happy to sign a change order that references the existing MSA.

Attached: Orchid_Change_Request_v1.docx (summary), OrderForm_ORC-2024-0042_v3.xlsx (current + requested).

Timing: procurement would like a signed change order the week of June 16 to meet our rollout schedule. Can you confirm Redwood's path (commercial + legal) and an estimated turnaround?

Appreciate it — we can be flexible on the exact SLA language but will need confirmation on audit logs and data retention to satisfy our security team.

Best,
Priya Desai
Head of Cloud Ops, Orchid AI
priya@orchid.ai
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Priya Desai <priya@orchid.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 07 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: add capacity + rate adjustment (Orchid)

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments.

High level: commercial is likely OK with moving the incremental volume onto the Tier 3 price ladder; we typically handle this with a change order (Order Form update + short commercial memo) that references the MSA. Legal will need to review for any downstream implications (MSA Exhibits and SLA references).

Action plan I propose:
- I will draft a one-page Change Order that: updates the Order Form quantities, shows the new effective unit price for the increment, and references the existing MSA/Order Form IDs.
- Marissa, can your team confirm whether we need an explicit MSA Exhibit A redline for the SOW or whether the change order can live as a standalone commercial amendment? Also please confirm if we require any edits to the Data Processing Addendum for the added throughput.
- Kar, can you confirm commercial approval for the Tier 3 pricing on the 200k increment and whether we want to add a 60-day ramp credit?

Timeline target: draft change order to Orchid by EOD Mon Jun 9, legal redline back by Tue Jun 10, target signing w/ DocuSign open by June 16. If any of you see blockers to that cadence speak up now.

I've started a barebones draft (attached) to speed review: proposed_change_order_draft.docx (stub).

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 08 Jun 2025 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: add capacity + rate adjustment (Orchid)

Quick note — commercial is OK to price the 200k at Tier 3 for the incremental units, provided we:
- confirm the billing start date (we should align to July 1)
- confirm usage measurement window and any lookback for credits
- include a 60-day ramp credit (50% credit on the incremental units for first 60 days) to help their rollout.

No objection to standalone change order referencing the MSA. I'll sign off on the pricing in the draft.

Also: please include a DocuSign signing order: Orchid procurement -> Orchid legal -> Redwood commercial -> Redwood legal. That usually helps their internal ops.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Jun 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: add capacity + rate adjustment (Orchid)

Lauren / Karthik — I reviewed the attachments and the draft change order. A few legal points to surface before we send anything to Orchid for signature: 

1) MSA cross-references: the draft references Exhibit A (SOW) and Exhibit C (Order Form). If we keep the change as a standalone change order, we must explicitly state that no other MSA terms are amended. That prevents unintended updates to acceptance criteria.

2) SLA & audit logs: Orchid asked about audit logs / retention. Our standard MSA references audit logging in Section 5.4 — we need to confirm with Product whether the increased throughput triggers any different retention or logging costs. If not, we should add a short carveout sentence in the change order: "No change to logging or retention obligations; customer may request audit copies subject to standard fees."

3) Data Processing Addendum (DPA): increasing throughput could change subcontractor exposure if we route traffic to burst pools in a different region. Product to confirm whether this will touch APAC egress. If so, legal will need to add an API-level data routing note.

4) Indemnity/cap on liability: the incremental revenue is material over time. Recommend leaving existing liability caps intact and not opening up broader indemnity. If customer pushes back, we can include a time-limited carveout for the incremental capacity only.

I'll prepare a redline of Exhibit A (if needed) plus a short change order template that includes the pricing table and the 60-day ramp credit language. Attaching: MSA_exhibitA_redline-lgl_v1.docx (redline stub).

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
